task1.title: Shakefield town changes
task1.prompt: The diagram below shows the changes of the town named Shakefield from 1995 until now.

changes: Farm land in the northeast replaced by a Golf Course and Tennis Course
Public park in the center-right replaced by Holiday homes
Sport area in the west replaced by a Restaurant
Fish market in the southwest replaced by Apartment buildings
Morning fish boat area in the sea replaced by Yacht anchorages
Car park added along the road on the eastern side
chartDesc.overview: Between 1995 and the present, Shakefield transformed from a small coastal fishing and farming town into a tourist-oriented resort featuring enhanced residential options and recreational facilities.
unchanged: Coffee shop south of the hotel
keyFeatures: Replacement of Farm land with a Golf Course and Tennis Course
Conversion of the Public park into Holiday homes
Replacement of the Fish market and Morning fish boat with Apartments and Yachts
Expansion of the Hotel and Housing area
Replacement of Sport facilities with a Restaurant

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparison where relevant.
task1.sampleBand5:
The diagram shows the changes in Shakefield town from 1995 to now. Overall, there have been some big changes to the town's facilities.

In 1995, there was a shop and a school in the north. Now, the shop has gone, and there is housing instead. The school is still there. In the south, there was a park. This has changed to become a shopping centre. A new park has been built next to the shopping centre.

In the middle of the town, the river is still there. On the east side, there was a factory. Now, the factory is housing. On the west side, the houses are still there. There is also a new bridge over the river. The main change is there are more houses and shops and less factories.
task1.sampleBand6:
The diagram shows how the town of Shakefield changed between 1995 and the present day. Overall, the town became more developed, with new facilities and the removal of some older features.

In 1995, Shakefield was a smaller town. There was a park in the north, a factory in the south, and houses in the middle. The factory was quite large. There was also a river running through the town. By the present day, the factory has been replaced with a shopping center. The park remained in the same location, but it was made smaller because some new houses were build next to it.

Furthermore, the river is still there, but a bridge has been built across it, which gives access to the new shopping center from the houses. In addition to the new houses near the park, more houses have been built where the factory used to be before the shopping center was constructed. The town has clearly grown and become more modern.
task1.sampleBand7:
The diagrams illustrate the transformation of the town of Shakefield between 1995 and the present day. Overall, the town has experienced considerable development, particularly in infrastructure and residential areas, with a noticeable shift away from agriculture.

In 1995, Shakefield was primarily characterized by farmland to the north and west of the town center. The town center itself consisted of housing and shops. By the present day, the farmland to the north has been replaced by a large golf course and a new housing estate. The farmland to the west has been converted into an industrial area.

The town center has also seen significant changes. The number of houses has increased, and a new school has been built. Furthermore, transport infrastructure has been improved with the construction of a ring road around the town, presumably to alleviate traffic congestion. While the shops remain in the town center, their size or number is not readily apparent from the diagrams. In summary, Shakefield has become more urbanized, with less agricultural land and better facilities for its residents.
task1.sampleBand8:

In 1995, Shakefield was characterized by a large factory in the north and farmland to the south. A river ran through the town centre. task1.sampleBand9:
The diagram illustrates the transformation of Shakefield town between 1995 and the present day. Overall, the town has undergone significant development, primarily involving expansion and modernisation of infrastructure and amenities.

In 1995, Shakefield was a relatively small town characterised by a limited number of residential areas and a prominent industrial zone to the east. task1.sampleAnswer:
The two maps compare the town of Shakefield as it appeared in 1995 with its current layout. Overall, the town has undergone significant urban development, transitioning from a primarily residential and industrial area into a more commercialized and accessible urban center. Most notable is the expansion of transport infrastructure and the replacement of industrial zones with commercial facilities.

In 1995, the north-western part of the town was dominated by a large industrial estate, which has since been demolished and replaced with a modern shopping mall. Adjacent to this, the residential housing in the north-east has remained largely intact, though a new primary school has been constructed nearby to cater to the local population. The central area, which previously featured a small park, has been redesigned to include a larger recreational space with an added fountain and seating areas.

Infrastructure improvements are also highly visible. The narrow road running through the town center in 1995 has been widened into a dual carriageway. Furthermore, a new train station has been built on the southern edge of the town, connected to the center by a dedicated bus lane. The old woodland area in the south-east has been partially cleared to make way for a new apartment complex, reflecting the town's growing housing demands.

Yangi uy-joyning sharqiy qismida savdo markazi qurildi, bu esa kengaygan aholining ehtiyojlarini qondirishga qaratilgan.

Shuni ta'kidlash joizki, shaharning umumiy tuzilishi yanada tartibli va zamonaviy bo'lib, uning avvalgi sanoat va qishloq xo'jaligi yo'nalishidan uzoqlashishini aks ettiradi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, Shakefield sanoat va qishloq xo'jaligi shaharchasidan takomillashtirilgan qulayliklar va infratuzilmaga ega bo'lgan asosan turar-joy hududiga o'tishni boshidan kechirdi.

task2.title: Oil exploration in remote areas
task2.prompt: The global demand for oil and gas is increasing. Some believe that we should therefore encourage the exploitation of remote areas. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
task2.instruction: Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
task2.sampleBand5:
Nowadays, the demand for oil and gas is getting more and more. Some people think it is good to try and find these things in faraway places. This essay will talk about the good things and bad things about this idea.

One good thing is that it could give us more energy. If we find more oil and gas, then we will have more fuel for our cars and power for our homes. This is important for keeping the economy going. Also, it could make some countries richer because they can sell the oil and gas to other countries. It creates job opportunities.

But there are also bad things. One big problem is that it can hurt the environment. When they dig for oil and gas, they can damage the land and the water. This can kill plants and animals, and it can also pollute the air. Remote areas are often very beautiful and untouched, so it is a shame to ruin them. Also, it can be very expensive to get oil and gas from these places. It needs new technology and it can be difficult to get the oil and gas back.

To sum up, finding oil and gas in remote areas has both good and bad points. While it can give us more energy and money, it can also damage the environment and cost a lot. I think it is important to think about all of these things before we decide to do it. We need to find a way to get energy without hurting the planet too much.
task2.sampleBand6:
The increasing global demand for oil and gas has led to suggestions that we should exploit remote areas to meet this need. While there may be some benefits to this approach, I believe that the disadvantages are more significant.

One potential advantage is that exploiting remote areas could boost economic growth. This is because new jobs would be created in the extraction and transportation of these resources. For example, communities near oil fields could benefit from increased employment opportunities. Furthermore, the revenue generated from the sale of oil and gas could be used to fund public services, such as education and healthcare. However, these benefits are often short-term and may not outweigh the long-term costs.

On the other hand, there are several disadvantages to exploiting remote areas. Firstly, it can have a devastating impact on the environment. The extraction of oil and gas can lead to deforestation, pollution, and the destruction of natural habitats. Furthermore, the transportation of these resources can also pose a risk of oil spills and other environmental disasters. Secondly, exploiting remote areas can disrupt the lives of indigenous communities who depend on these areas for their livelihoods. These communities may be displaced from their homes and lose access to traditional hunting and fishing grounds. In addition to this, the influx of workers into these areas can lead to social problems, such as crime and drug abuse.

In conclusion, while the exploitation of remote areas may offer some economic benefits, the environmental and social costs are too high. We should focus on developing renewable energy sources and reducing our reliance on fossil fuels instead of damaging these fragile environments. It is important to consider the long-term consequences of our actions and prioritize the protection of our planet and its people.
task2.sampleBand7:
With the global demand for oil and gas constantly on the rise, the question of whether we should exploit remote areas to meet this demand is a pressing one. While there are certain advantages to pursuing this course of action, I believe that the disadvantages ultimately outweigh them.

One key advantage is the potential for economic growth. Exploiting resources in remote areas can create jobs, stimulate local economies, and generate significant revenue for governments. Furthermore, it could reduce a nation’s reliance on foreign energy sources, enhancing its energy security. For instance, the development of oil fields in the North Sea, although challenging, transformed the UK economy in the late 20th century. This demonstrates that resource exploitation can indeed bring about considerable economic benefits. However, these benefits must be weighed against the potential environmental and social costs.

The disadvantages of exploiting remote areas are numerous and significant. Environmentally, these regions are often fragile and pristine ecosystems that are highly vulnerable to damage from resource extraction. Oil spills, deforestation, and habitat destruction can have devastating and long-lasting consequences. For example, the extraction of oil from the Amazon rainforest has led to widespread environmental damage and the displacement of indigenous communities. Moreover, the infrastructure required for resource extraction, such as roads and pipelines, can further fragment habitats and disrupt wildlife.

Socially, the exploitation of remote areas can also have negative impacts on local communities. The influx of workers and the disruption of traditional ways of life can lead to social unrest and cultural erosion. Additionally, the benefits of resource extraction may not always be equitably distributed, leading to inequality and resentment. While companies may promise jobs and development, these promises are not always fulfilled, leaving communities worse off than before. In light of these considerations, the social costs can be substantial.

In conclusion, while the exploitation of remote areas for oil and gas may offer some economic advantages and enhanced energy security, the environmental and social disadvantages are considerable. Therefore, on balance, I believe that the disadvantages outweigh the advantages, and that we should prioritize alternative energy sources and more sustainable practices.
task2.sampleBand8:
The escalating global demand for oil and gas has sparked debate regarding the exploitation of resources in remote and often environmentally sensitive areas. While tapping into these reserves could offer certain advantages, I believe that the potential disadvantages, particularly concerning environmental degradation and social impact, substantially outweigh any perceived benefits.

One potential advantage lies in increased energy security. Accessing previously untapped reserves in remote regions could reduce reliance on politically unstable nations and bolster domestic energy production. This could lead to lower energy prices and a more stable economy. Furthermore, such projects often create jobs in the construction and energy sectors, offering economic opportunities to local communities. However, these benefits are often short-lived and disproportionately distributed, with multinational corporations reaping the majority of the profits.

Conversely, the disadvantages of exploiting remote areas for oil and gas are considerable. The most significant concern is the environmental impact. Drilling and extraction processes can lead to devastating oil spills, habitat destruction, and pollution of water sources. Remote areas are often home to unique ecosystems and endangered species that are particularly vulnerable to such disturbances. The construction of infrastructure, such as roads and pipelines, further fragments habitats and disrupts wildlife migration patterns. Moreover, the carbon footprint associated with extracting and transporting these resources contributes significantly to climate change, exacerbating existing environmental problems.

Beyond the environmental consequences, the social impact on indigenous communities must also be considered. These communities often have deep cultural and spiritual connections to the land, which can be irrevocably disrupted by resource extraction. The influx of workers can lead to social problems such as increased crime rates and the spread of diseases. Furthermore, indigenous communities may not receive adequate compensation or benefits from these projects, leading to displacement and marginalization. It is crucial to acknowledge that while economic gains may be achieved, they often come at the expense of cultural heritage and traditional ways of life. A more sustainable approach involves investing in renewable energy sources and reducing overall energy consumption.

In conclusion, while the exploitation of remote areas for oil and gas may offer some short-term economic benefits, the long-term environmental and social costs are too high. The potential for environmental damage, disruption of indigenous communities, and contribution to climate change render this approach unsustainable. A more responsible path forward involves prioritizing renewable energy and implementing stringent environmental regulations to protect our planet's fragile ecosystems.
task2.sampleBand9:
The increasing global demand for oil and gas has prompted suggestions that exploiting resources in remote and previously untouched areas is necessary. While there may be some economic benefits to this approach, I believe that the disadvantages, particularly environmental and social costs, significantly outweigh any potential advantages.

One potential advantage of exploiting remote areas for oil and gas is the economic boost it can provide. Such ventures often generate employment opportunities for local communities, injecting capital into otherwise economically depressed regions. Furthermore, the extraction and sale of these resources can contribute significantly to national GDP, funding public services and infrastructure projects. Advocates argue that these economic gains are essential for development and improving living standards, particularly in countries heavily reliant on fossil fuel exports.

However, the disadvantages of this approach are far more compelling. The environmental impact of extracting resources from remote areas is often devastating. Fragile ecosystems, such as the Arctic tundra or rainforests, are particularly vulnerable to the disruption caused by drilling, pipelines, and increased human activity. Oil spills, habitat destruction, and the release of greenhouse gases are just some of the potential consequences. Moreover, the long-term ecological damage can be irreversible, threatening biodiversity and contributing to climate change. The social costs can also be considerable. Indigenous communities, who often rely on these areas for their traditional livelihoods and cultural practices, may be displaced or otherwise negatively impacted by resource extraction. This can lead to social unrest, loss of cultural identity, and increased inequality.

In conclusion, while the exploitation of remote areas for oil and gas may offer some short-term economic advantages, these are dwarfed by the significant environmental and social costs. A more sustainable and responsible approach would be to prioritize investment in renewable energy sources and energy efficiency measures, rather than pursuing environmentally damaging and socially disruptive resource extraction in fragile ecosystems. A paradigm shift towards sustainability is not merely desirable but essential for the long-term well-being of both the planet and its inhabitants. The purported economic benefits simply do not justify the inherent risks.
task2.sampleAnswer:
In the face of burgeoning global energy requirements, the proposal to extract fossil fuels from previously untouched remote regions, such as the Arctic or deep-sea environments, has become a point of intense contention. While this approach offers significant economic and energy security benefits, I believe that the catastrophic environmental risks and the urgent need for a transition to renewable energy mean that the disadvantages ultimately outweigh the advantages.

On the one hand, the primary argument for exploiting remote areas is the maintenance of energy stability. As traditional reserves are depleted, tapping into new sources ensures that the global economy does not suffer from crippling energy shortages or price hikes. Furthermore, such projects often bring immense economic prosperity to the investing nations, creating thousands of high-skilled jobs and stimulating technological innovation in extraction techniques. For countries heavily reliant on energy imports, this move toward self-sufficiency is a powerful incentive.

However, the environmental cost of such ventures is often irreversible. Remote areas are frequently home to fragile ecosystems that are highly sensitive to industrial activity. An oil spill in the Arctic, for instance, would be nearly impossible to contain or clean up due to the extreme conditions, leading to the long-term destruction of unique biodiversity. Moreover, encouraging further fossil fuel exploitation distracts from the vital goal of achieving carbon neutrality. Instead of investing billions into accessing difficult-to-reach oil, those resources would be better spent on accelerating the development of solar, wind, and hydrogen technologies, which are the only sustainable solutions to the climate crisis.

In conclusion, although the exploitation of remote areas provides a short-term fix for energy demands and significant economic gains, the potential for ecological disaster is too great. The long-term survival of the planet depends on our ability to move away from fossil fuels entirely, making the pursuit of remote oil reserves a regressive and dangerous strategy.
task2.uzSampleBand5:
Hozirgi kunda neft va gazga bo'lgan talab tobora ortib bormoqda. Ba'zi odamlar buni urinib, topishga harakat qilish uzoq joylarda yaxshi deb o'ylashadi. Ushbu insho ushbu fikrning yaxshi va yomon tomonlari haqida gapiradi.

Bir yaxshi tomoni shundaki, bu bizga ko'proq energiya berishi mumkin. Agar biz ko'proq neft va gaz topsak, unda bizda mashinalarimiz uchun ko'proq yoqilg'i va uylarimiz uchun quvvat bo'ladi. Bu iqtisodiyotni saqlab turish uchun muhim. Bundan tashqari, bu ba'zi mamlakatlarni boyroq qilishi mumkin, chunki ular neft va gazni boshqa mamlakatlarga sotishlari mumkin. Bu ish o'rinlarini yaratadi.

Ammo yomon tomonlari ham bor. Bir katta muammo shundaki, bu atrof-muhitga zarar etkazishi mumkin. Ular neft va gaz qaziyotganda, ular er va suvga zarar etkazishi mumkin. Bu o'simliklar va hayvonlarni o'ldirishi mumkin, shuningdek, havoni ifloslantirishi mumkin. Uzoq hududlar ko'pincha juda chiroyli va daxlsiz bo'ladi, shuning uchun ularni buzish achinarli. Bundan tashqari, bu joylardan neft va gaz olish juda qimmatga tushishi mumkin. Unga yangi texnologiya kerak va neft va gazni qaytarib olish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, uzoq hududlarda neft va gaz topishning ham yaxshi, ham yomon tomonlari bor. Bu bizga ko'proq energiya va pul berishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, u atrof-muhitga zarar etkazishi va qimmatga tushishi mumkin. Menimcha, bu juda muhim buni qilishga qaror qilishdan oldin bularning barchasi haqida o'ylab ko'rish. Biz sayyoraga juda ko'p zarar etkazmasdan energiya olish yo'lini topishimiz kerak.
task2.uzSampleBand6:
Neft va gazga bo'lgan global talabning ortishi ushbu ehtiyojni qondirish uchun olis hududlardan foydalanishimiz kerak degan takliflarga olib keldi. Ushbu yondashuvning ba'zi afzalliklari bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, menimcha, kamchiliklari sezilarliroq.

Potensial afzalliklardan biri shundaki, olis hududlardan foydalanish iqtisodiy o'sishni rag'batlantirishi mumkin. Buning sababi shundaki, ushbu resurslarni qazib olish va tashishda yangi ish o'rinlari yaratiladi. Misol uchun, neft konlari yaqinidagi jamoalar bandlik imkoniyatlarining ortishidan foyda ko'rishlari mumkin. Bundan tashqari, neft va gazni sotishdan tushgan daromad ta'lim va sog'liqni saqlash kabi davlat xizmatlarini moliyalashtirish uchun ishlatilishi mumkin. Biroq, bu imtiyozlar ko'pincha qisqa muddatli bo'ladi va uzoq muddatli xarajatlardan ustun kelmasligi mumkin.

Boshqa tomondan, olis hududlardan foydalanishning bir nechta kamchiliklari mavjud. Birinchidan, bu atrof-muhitga halokatli ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin. Neft va gaz qazib olish o'rmonlarning kesilishiga, ifloslanishga va tabiiy yashash joylarining yo'q qilinishiga olib kelishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ushbu resurslarni tashish neft to'kilishi va boshqa ekologik ofatlar xavfini ham keltirib chiqarishi mumkin. Ikkinchidan, olis hududlardan foydalanish ushbu hududlarga tirikchilik uchun bog'liq bo'lgan mahalliy jamoalarning hayotini buzishi mumkin.
